title: Apply, pass inspection, and price compliance into every pack
course_title: Business Registration & Compliance for Product Makers: NAFDAC, SON and Safe Production

say: Apply, pass inspection, and price compliance into every pack.
This is the video for module two of Business Registration and Compliance: the application, the production room and the numbers.
NAFDAC's small business procedure has six stages, with a stated timeline of ninety working days. Doing each stage well stops your file from stalling.

say: Samples are collected and sent to the laboratory. Plan ahead: ninety working days is about 18 weeks. For example, Chiamaka adds 2 weeks of buffer and applies 20 weeks before her trade fair.

say: A designated room is used only for production, not a family kitchen. Contamination happens when dirty and clean things cross, so materials move one way.
For example, Grace in Jos converts a 3 by 4 metre room for chin-chin. Its back door faced the compound toilet, so she sealed it. Raw materials sit on a shelf by the front door.

items: Raw material store
Weighing and preparation
Processing or mixing
Cooling and filling
Labelling and packed storage

say: Next comes the mixing table, then frying under a screened window.

say: Then the cooling rack, and the packing table in the far corner. Waste leaves by a route that does not pass the packing table.
She adds a handwashing point with soap, a pedal bin with a lid, and shelves 15 cm off the floor.

say: Walk into your own room as if you were the inspector. Is it clean and screened? Is there water and soap for handwashing? Are workers in aprons and hair covers, with certificates on file?
Are materials off the floor and labelled? Are your formula, batch records, cleaning log and fumigation certificate ready in one show file? And is there product from a normal batch for samples?

panel.heading: What the inspector looks at
items: Room: clean, screened, no opening to toilet
Water and soap for handwashing
Aprons, hair covers, medical certificates
Materials off the floor, labelled, receipts
Formula, batch records, cleaning log
Product from a normal batch for samples

say: Keep gas cylinders outside or in a ventilated spot, away from the frying area, with a working regulator and hose.

cards.d: Outside or ventilated, away from frying, with a working regulator and hose.
Keep a fire blanket or extinguisher within reach.
Never mix bleach with other cleaners. Store chemicals apart from ingredients, labelled.

say: Never mix bleach with other cleaners, because some combinations release harmful gas. Store cleaning chemicals on a separate shelf, in their original labelled containers.
And nobody works on production while sick with vomiting, diarrhoea or fever.

say: Grace lists her compliance costs: the NAFDAC fee from her payment advice, medical tests, fumigation, label redesign and room improvements. Fees can change, so always confirm them, and get real quotes.

card.title: Compliance cost per pack
card.note: Fees can change. Quotes are illustrative.

say: They add up to 206,737.50 naira. Repeating fumigation and medical tests in year two adds 70,000, making 276,737.50.

card.title: Compliance cost per pack
card.note: Fees can change. Quotes are illustrative.

say: Over two years she sells 7,200 packs. Divided out, that is about 38.44 naira a pack, rounded up to 40.

card.title: Compliance cost per pack
card.note: Fees can change. Quotes are illustrative.

say: With her other costs of 620 naira, each pack now costs 660. At 1,000 naira, she still makes 340 profit.
At only 50 packs a month, the same costs would be about 231 naira a pack. That is why you list your best sellers first.

say: To remember. Plan about 18 weeks plus a buffer. Book the inspection on a production day. Keep a designated room with one-way flow.
Keep gas away from heat and never mix bleach. And spread compliance cost over the units you sell.
